summary: Alatrofloxacin was pulled from the market in the United States and the European Union starting in 2006 because of liver harm [3]. A small computer model, rather than tests on people, gave it a high risk score of 82 for the liver and a low risk score of 18 for the heart [M]. A similar medicine named Trovafloxacin was also pulled from the market in the United States and two other countries for liver harm, and it carries a boxed warning in the United States [4]. Another related drug, Temafloxacin, was pulled from the worldwide market in 1992 for blood-related harm and metabolic harm, which refers to problems with how the body processes energy [5].
